newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate surges on late speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate surges on late speculation.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates reversed an early decline to close up 150 basis points at 23.50 percent on Tuesday on what traders said was a late speculative spike.

"The market was very speculative. You have one big player with most of the paper, and another with most of the cash, and they need to square positions for the central bank's cutoff. The one with the money has the advantage," a trader said.
Wednesday sees the deadline for banks to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with Banco de Mexico.

Dealers said forecasts of imminent hikes in domestic primary rates also fueled late gains in secondary rates. surveyed by Reuters showed they forecast on average Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes at 20.77 percent.
This would be an increase of 147 basis points since last week's auction.
Banco de Mexico drained 1.591 billion pesos from the secondary market through three direct Cetes sales coupled with three repos, which, traders said, also exerted upside pressure on market rates.
Cetes overnight rates had earlier dipped 50 basis points to 21.50 percent on what dealers said was a positive reaction to low inflation data released late on Monday. Overnight rates
on bank paper climbed 110 basis points to 24.15 percent.
Liquidity of 309 million pesos was programed to return to the system on Wednesday from prior central bank participation.
